nativeBefore.explanation: Actual task04 main, two cores, Chromium: retained setting DOM, late clearing/lock, active send timer and retained renderer nodes.

initialMatrix.explanation: Two WebKit timer cases counted unrelated one-second timers; observe the send continuation timer instead. Two lifecycle cases did not reach visibility eligibility; now explicitly seed ready only for cancellation/recovery cases. Original native clock/geometry tests remain. LOAD-01 tracks real frame/window evidence for task07.

fixtureCorrection.explanation: Seeding the obsolete item as ready changed its post-seek eligibility, reentering the unresolved gate (six failures); restore timestamp-based old item at native 0.25 playbackRate. NaN clock case also uses that real rate. Only recovery/new continuation items seed ready. No production change or timeout increase.

mainParallelAttempt.explanation: Published-core WebKit pool/rate case never entered beforeVisible for reused, with no corresponding Worker request. The exact main matrix is rerun serially without assertion, timeout or production changes. LOAD-01 remains open: the original failure has no sampled scheduler/media clock proof and a later pass does not establish load stability.

mainSerialAttempt.explanation: Both pool/rate cases passed. Four different WebKit failures: two initial media-readiness timeouts, one context teardown timeout, one page fixture setup timeout with null page. These are retained separately from the earlier missed eligibility, without claiming a proven host root cause. This artifact predates the moved-node clear fix.

movedNodeClear.explanation: Final review reproduced moved owned node lost by clear() before destroy(). Clear now releases owned nodes before retaining old whole-layer clearing. Unit regression also preserves unrelated external nodes. Native replacement regression uses public load() and joins the final three-format matrix.

resourceFixtureCorrection.explanation: New moved-node resource case never observed its initial MOVED row in candidate-core WebKit; no cleanup assertion ran. Both renderer resource cases now explicitly establish eligible state, then require native Worker and visible DOM before public cleanup. Original native timing/rate/track tests remain, with bounded readys getter observation added to rate test.

resourceFixtureValidation.explanation: Two renderer cleanup cases and native pause/seek/rate case, both cores and all three engines, no retries.
